title: Introduce Thrifty Queue Sculptor and Quant Compatibility Coordinator
author: Asha Patel
release_notes:
- Add Thrifty Queue Sculptor: microqueue shaping service to reduce small-batch overhead and cold KV-cache misses.
- Add Quant Compatibility Coordinator: runtime policy to route requests to compatible quantized variants with graceful fallback.
- New telemetry: queue_shaper.* and quant_coordinator.* metrics and a CLI dry-run mode (thriftyctl).
description:
Motivation: Customers with spiky, low-amplitude traffic spend disproportionately on per-token cost because many requests land in tiny microqueues (1-2 requests) and trigger KV-cache cold starts or conservative batch sizing. This PR introduces a lightweight, tenant-aware Queue Sculptor that shapes microqueues and nudges requests into efficient batch footprints while respecting latency SLOs, plus a Quant Compatibility Coordinator to ensure safe fallbacks between quantized model variants when shaping changes request routing.

Summary of changes:
- Runtime: add queue_sculptor service that maintains short-lived micro-queues per-tenant and applies shaping policies (time-window, soft-hold, priority decay). The sculptor exposes an API for batch hints to the batcher and a feedback hook for telemetry.
- Quant: introduce quant_compat coordinator that tracks compatibility matrix for model variants (fp16/q4/q8) and performs fast compatibility checks before routing; includes fallback policy DSL (latency-first, cost-first, safety-first).
- CLI: thriftyctl profile-dryrun to simulate shaping and quant fallback effects against historical traces.
- Telemetry: new metrics and events (queue_shaper.hold_ms, queue_shaper.effective_batch_size, quant_coordinator.fallbacks, quant_coordinator.compatibility_errors) and dashboard skeleton in observability-pack.
- Tests: unit tests for policy evaluation, integration tests with the batcher harness, and a synthetic loadbench to validate cost/latency tradeoffs.

Checklist:
- [x] Design doc linked (Linear ENG-4367) and reviewed by runtime and inference teams.
- [x] Unit & integration tests added.
- [x] Telemetry and dashboards stubbed; tagging and metrics names reviewed.
- [x] Backwards-compatible: sculptor is off by default and requires an opt-in tenant flag.

Testing summary:
- Local unit tests: 142 passed, 0 failed.
- Integration (batcher + sculptor): synthetic traces showed 22%-30% lower unit token cost for microburst workloads with negligible p95 latency regression (<5ms increase).
- Nightly dry-run via thriftyctl against replay stored traces: behavior validated for tenants with mixed model families.

Rollout plan:
1) Merge behind feature flag off by default. 2) Enable sculptor in a small set of test tenants (canary) with monitoring alerts on fallback counts. 3) Expand to more tenants when fallbacks are under threshold and p95 latency meets SLO.

Known limitations and follow-ups:
- Current sculptor uses simple exponential backoff heuristics; follow-up (ENG-4412) will add ML-driven shaping profiles.
- Quant compatibility is conservative for novel model families; requires an onboarding step (compat matrix generator) in model-registry.

Related work: shares goals with recent batch-cache and prefill efforts but takes a different approach by operating at queue shaping time rather than only post-batch heuristics. Linear: ENG-4367, ENG-4412.

Notes: This PR purposefully aims for minimal runtime surface area: no required runtime changes for tenants that don't opt in. Metrics, CLI, and dashboard scaffolding are included so SRE and observability can validate the economics impact before broad rollout.

review_conversation:
Ryan Cho: Can we make the soft-hold window tenant-configurable?
Asha: Yes — implemented tenant-level override with safe upper bound (200ms) and default 30ms. Added doc and unit test.
Marta Kovács: The quant fallback metric looks high on the synthetic run for the BERT family — can you add per-model logging to understand root cause?
Asha: Added per-model fallback tags and a small sampling flag to limit cardinality. Re-ran dry-run, fallback rate fell by 40% after disabling an aggressive cost-first policy for BERT.
Derek Nguyen: Approve after addressing telemetry naming and adding a CLI dry-run summary.
Marta Kovács: Approved.
Merge approvals: 2/3 approvals; one follow-up comment captured in ENG-4412.

notes_for_ops: Enable feature flag 'queue_sculptor.v1' per-tenant via tenant-config service. Watch metrics: queue_shaper.effective_batch_size, quant_coordinator.fallbacks, batcher.latency.p95. Escalate if fallbacks > 0.5% for a tenant over 30m window.
testing_instructions: 1) Build runtime image and enable queue_sculptor feature flag on a test tenant. 2) Run thriftyctl profile-dryrun --tenant <id> --trace <trace-id> and inspect dry-run report in /tmp/thrifty_dryrun.json. 3) Validate metrics in the canary dashboard.
